note: After Ruelle's 1970 revision of the Ethiopian Macrotermes (pp. 374—376; alate, major soldier neotype, minor soldier, major worker). The original is in English. In the scanned text layer the measurement tables of that revision retain only the item names and the values are missing as a whole, so only the measurement given in the running text (major worker head width) is kept here; the soldier and alate entries are morphological descriptions without figures. Nomenclatural points: the type specimen of Smeathman 1781 is lost and Ruelle selected a neotype from Njala, Sierra Leone; records of 'natalensis' from within the range of this species in the older literature should be referred to it, while 'bellicosus' was long misapplied to what are now M. subhyalinus and M. mossambicus.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A large Macrotermes. Soldier mandibles not upturned at the tip, the head in lateral view rather flat with the upper and lower margins nearly parallel, the postmentum not projecting; pronotum relatively small, the notch of the anterior margin deeper than that of the posterior margin, the anterolateral corners sharper than in M. subhyalinus and the sides nearly straight; the thoracic tergites less strongly sclerotized than in M. subhyalinus. Alate head dark brown, the pronotum with a pale T-shaped mark, the fontanelle at the tip of a small elevation with no median ridge in front of it, the frons flat and not depressed around the fontanelle.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head dark brown, the dorsum with numerous setae surrounded at their bases by pale dots. Anteclypeus paler than the head, with a dark median line in the middle; pronotum concolorous with the head, with a pale T-shaped mark (as in M. subhyalinus); abdominal tergites dark brown; wings semi-transparent, tinged with smoky. Vertex rounded; frons flat, not depressed around the fontanelle; fontanelle distinct, at the tip of a small elevation, with no median ridge in front of it (contrary to M. natalensis). Compound eyes broadly oval and large, but less circular than in M. subhyalinus and less bulging than in M. mossambicus; ocelli nearly circular, their distance from the compound eyes not exceeding the diameter of the ocellus itself, the original value being a fraction that is illegible in the scan and therefore not entered. Anteclypeus wider and more inflated than in M. subhyalinus. Antennae 19-segmented, segment 3 longer than segments 2 and 4. Anterior margin of the pronotum straight, the posterior margin broadly concave, the relative width greater than in M. subhyalinus.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Major soldier (neotype): head yellowish brown, mandibles black with red at the base; postmentum darker than the cheeks below it. Pronotum paler than the head, the mesonotum and metanotum still paler and close to the colour of the abdominal tergites; legs yellow, the tibiae not darker than the femora. Head in dorsal view nearly rectangular, the sides almost straight and only slightly narrowing forwards; mandibles not upturned at the tip, the left mandible wider than the right and slightly more incurved, its inner margin finely serrate when seen from below. In lateral view the head is rather flat, the upper and lower margins nearly parallel, the postmentum not projecting. Antennae 17-segmented, segment 3 almost twice as long as segment 2, segment 4 and the following segments shorter than segment 2, segment 1 as long as segment 3; setae on the dorsum of the head sparse, more numerous on the postmentum. Labrum oval, its transparent end triangular with the sides nearly concave. Pronotum relatively small, the notch of the anterior margin deeper than that of the posterior margin, the anterolateral corners sharper than in M. subhyalinus, the sides nearly straight; mesonotum distinctly narrower than the pronotum and only slightly narrower than the metanotum, its lateral margins with a blunt point; posterior margin of the metanotum convex; the thoracic tergites less strongly sclerotized than in M. subhyalinus. Minor soldier: head slightly paler than in the major soldier, mandibles dark reddish brown; thoracic tergites paler than the head and close to the colour of the abdominal tergites; head more slender, mandibles finer and more symmetrical, the left mandible distinctly serrate; sides of the transparent end of the labrum convex; among the thoracic tergites the pronotum is the widest and the mesonotum the narrowest, the metanotum not distinctly wider than the mesonotum. Antennae of both soldier forms 17—18-segmented; postmentum narrow, at least 2 times and often up to 3 times as long as wide, the sides nearly parallel or concave.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Major worker head brown, without the reddish tinge of M. subhyalinus; the posterior margin of the head less rounded than in M. natalensis and M. subhyalinus. Head width 2.04—2.91 mm, mean 2.47 mm (204 specimens from 94 localities). Mandibles similar to those of the alate.
